paras: The killing of Fred Minge was the beating and drowning of a Black chef by sailors aboard the lake steamer "City of Toledo", reported from Toledo, Ohio, in August 1920. According to the only report found, the sailors attacked him after he denounced crew members who had taken part in recent riots, and threw him into the lake, where he drowned.

Minge worked as chef on the steamer "City of Toledo". The report links the attack to "the recent riot in Chicago and in the state of Michigan," in which, it said, sailors had taken part, but it gives no date for the riots or for the killing.

Minge "denounced the action of sailors" who had joined in those riots, and sailors on the steamer then beat him "unmerefically." They then tossed his body into the lake, where he drowned. The report names none of the sailors, does not state their number or race, and does not say where on the lake the steamer was.
No report of an arrest, inquest, or recovery of the body appears in the coverage.

The Iowa Bystander, a Black weekly, ran the story on 6 August 1920 as a three-sentence front-page brief under a Toledo dateline, headed "SAILORS TOSS DISABLED." The brief described Minge as a "Negro chef" and presented the killing as the sailors' answer to his protest against their part in the riots. No account appeared in the white papers searched, and no other Black paper carried the story or a follow-up.
